about: Which LLM writes or reads the next runtime move (`model_for_move`), and which Claude model runs each role of the desk for one operator request (`model_for_desk_role`, asked once per role in ONE Jev call, the role in `instructions.role`). Jev answers with a probability per candidate model; the runtime uses the top one only when the verdict clears the design bar, else RUNTIME.md runtime_model_default (moves) or desk_role_defaults (desk roles). A model choice never authorizes a trade: prices stay structured and set by code, and GUARDRAILS.md still decides. Criteria keys are RUNTIME.md aliases; the runtime sends only the candidates listed in runtime_models (Claude ones only for the desk).

instructions.question: Which candidate model should handle the move described by `move_kind`, given `value_at_risk_primas`, `tick_seconds`, `seconds_left_in_tick`, `counterparty_text_chars` and `injection_risk_flags`?
instructions.note: Move kinds: `words` writes one short polite message inside a live tick (the price is attached by code, never by the model); `buy` and `sell` read a counterparty and phrase a move inside a live tick; `parse_request` turns an operator's sentence into a structured intent outside the tick loop; `steer` maps an operator's style instruction to bounded parameter deltas outside the tick loop. A reply that misses the tick is dropped, so speed dominates when `seconds_left_in_tick` is small (a 15 s Sunday tick leaves about 10 s for everything). Quality and resistance to prompt injection matter more when value at risk is high, when injection flags are present, or when the move is outside the tick loop. Cost matters for frequent moves such as `words`.

criteria.haiku-4-5: Claude Haiku 4.5: the fastest and cheapest candidate (about 1 s for a short reply; $1 / $5 per million input / output tokens). Right for `words` and other in-tick moves when seconds left are few, value at risk is small (under about 20 primas) and there are no injection flags. Weakest at ambiguous operator requests and at resisting adversarial counterparty text.
criteria.sonnet-5-5: Claude Sonnet 5.5: balanced speed, cost and quality (a few seconds at low effort; $2 / $10 per million tokens). Right for `parse_request` and `steer`, and for in-tick moves with moderate value at risk (about 20 to 60 primas) or a single injection flag when at least 8 s are left in the tick.
criteria.opus-5-5: Claude Opus 5.5: the strongest reasoning and the most robust to prompt injection, but slower and pricier ($4 / $20 per million tokens). Right for high-stakes moves (value at risk above about 60 primas), several injection flags, or ambiguous `parse_request` and `steer` moves outside the tick loop; wrong when fewer than about 10 s are left in the tick.
criteria.fable-5-1: Claude Fable 5.1: Anthropic's most capable widely released model, slowest and most expensive ($10 / $50 per million tokens). Right only for a rare, very high-stakes move outside the tick loop; never for `words` or any in-tick move.
criteria.gpt-6-1-sol: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol: near-frontier quality at lower cost than OpenAI's top model, with balanced speed (reasoning effort low). A second-opinion option for `parse_request` and `steer` outside the tick loop, or in-tick moves with more than 10 s left; latency is less proven in this runtime than the Claude candidates.

instructions.question: Which candidate model should run the desk role named in `role` for the operator request described by `value_at_risk_primas`, `counterparty_text_chars`, `injection_risk_flags`, `tick_seconds` and `seconds_left_in_tick`?
instructions.note: The desk is Team 1's trading assistant on the Claude Agent SDK. It runs outside the tick loop: `seconds_left_in_tick` is the whole time budget of one request (RUNTIME.md desk_timeout_s), `counterparty_text_chars` is the length of the operator's request, `value_at_risk_primas` is the largest price in it, and `injection_risk_flags` are prompt-injection shapes found in it (pasted counterparty text). Every write still passes GUARDRAILS.md twice and is a dry run unless the operator runs live, so a model never authorizes a trade: it decides how well the request is understood, how well the tools are chosen, and how robust the role is to injected text. Roles: `desk` is the orchestrator: it reads the request, answers simple questions with read tools (status, clock, rules, alerts, threads) and hands everything else to one subagent; it runs on every request and its turns add up. `strategist` reads market data (strategy, curves, tape, teams, book) and proposes at most three moves or bounded style deltas (`steer`); it never trades, and its reasoning is the longest. `buyer` reads the album and the price evidence, then calls dealer_buy or sell_bid with a max price at or below the card's value to us: the role that moves money. `seller` lists a duplicate (sell_list) or cancels an offer (sell_cancel), priced at the buyer's need and never below our value. `duelist` picks which live duel to move; our duel policy sets the price, so the model only routes. A request takes several turns with tool calls, so a model's per-turn latency multiplies, and the desk role's cost recurs on every request.

criteria.haiku-4-5: Claude Haiku 4.5: the fastest and cheapest candidate (about 1 to 2 s per short turn on the subscription; $1 / $5 per million input / output tokens). Right for roles that only route with little at stake: `duelist` (the policy sets the price) and the `desk` when the request is a plain read or a clear hand-off with low value at risk and no injection flags. Weakest at ambiguous requests, multi-step tool plans and adversarial text.
criteria.sonnet-5-5: Claude Sonnet 5.5: balanced speed, cost and quality (2.4 to 4 s per turn on the subscription; $2 / $10 per million tokens). Right for the `desk`, `buyer` and `seller` with low or moderate value at risk (up to about 60 primas) and at most one injection flag, and for a routine `strategist` read.
criteria.opus-5-5: Claude Opus 5.5: the strongest reasoning and the most robust to prompt injection, slower and pricier (3 to 4 s per turn on the subscription; $4 / $20 per million tokens). Right for `strategist` planning, for `buyer` and `seller` with value at risk above about 60 primas, for any role when the request carries several injection flags, and for the `desk` on an ambiguous request; the desk's time budget absorbs its latency.
criteria.fable-5-1: Claude Fable 5.1: Anthropic's most capable widely released model, the slowest and most expensive ($10 / $50 per million tokens). Right only for a rare, very high-stakes `strategist` or `buyer` request where a long answer is acceptable; never for `desk` or `duelist` routing.
